newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian premier urges northeast rebels for talks.
newsitem.headline: Indian premier urges northeast rebels for talks.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Tuesday urged separatist militants in the troubled northeast to take part in unconditional talks with the government.

"We appeal to the youths through you that the government of India is willing to hold unconditional talks with them, because they are not alien to us," Gujral told reporters at Guwahati, the main city in the state of Assam, while on a five-day tour of the region.
"Patience is very important. We are not challenging them. Thus there is no time fixed for them to come to peace talks," Gujral said.

Assam is one of the seven hilly states, often called the seven sisters, plagued by insurgency in an area predominantly populated by more than 200 ethnic tribes. The states are close to the borders of Burma, Bhutan, Tibet and Bangladesh.

On Monday, Gujral was greeted by a general strike called by the outlawed United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) as he arrived in the region, where political activists accuse New Delhi of ignoring regional development.
"I understand democracy, so I have not reacted to their strike," Gujral said.

Gujral said the federal government would formulate a separate industrial policy to speed up economic development in the region, while taking care to spend enough to maintain security against separatist violence.
"Peace brings progress and investments," he said.
A separate rebel group in the state of Manipur, the Revolutionary People's Front, called a strike for May 22, when Gujral is scheduled to visit that province.
In 1996, Gujral's predecessor, H.D. Deve Gowda, announced a 61 billion rupee ($1.7 billion) aid package for the northeastern region.
Formed in 1979, the ULFA is fighting for the independence of tea- and oil-rich Assam, the biggest state in the region.
The neighbouring states of Nagaland, Tripura and Manipur also have insurgent groups with tribal or vaguely Maoist ideologies.
Assam's ruling Asom Gana Parishad is one of 15 parties in Gujral's centre-left United Front coalition in New Delhi.
Some two dozen people were killed over the weekend in insurgency-related violence in the sprawling and remote northeastern region.
